# Format Conversion Workflowsvg image

Relevant source files

- [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md)
- [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml)
- [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py)

## Purpose and Scopesvg image

This document describes the workflow for converting context files between Markdown and HTML formats using the `md2html` and `html2md` commands. These conversion utilities enable bidirectional format transformation, allowing users to leverage format-specific advantages while maintaining data portability.

For information about creating context files from directories, see [Basic Packaging Workflow](/ray0404/Contexter/4.1-basic-packaging-workflow). For details on individual command usage and options, see [md2html](/ray0404/Contexter/5.4.2-md2html) and [html2md](/ray0404/Contexter/5.4.3-html2md).

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md34-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L34-L35) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py47-48](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L47-L48)

## Overviewsvg image

The format conversion system provides optional transformation between the two supported context file formats. Conversions preserve the complete project structure and file contents while adapting the presentation layer.

### Supported Conversionssvg image

| Conversion | Command | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Markdown → HTML | `md2html` | `.md` context file | `.html` context file |
| HTML → Markdown | `html2md` | `.html` context file | `.md` context file |

Both conversions are lossless with respect to project data—file paths, contents, and directory structure are preserved exactly. Only the serialization format changes.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md34-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L34-L35) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py31-48](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L31-L48)

## Conversion Architecturesvg image

### Command and Module Mappingsvg image

**Diagram: Format Conversion Module Structure**

The conversion system follows Contexter's standard architecture pattern with 1:1 command-to-module mapping. Both commands delegate to their respective implementation modules, which leverage `contexter_utils.py` for common operations.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py31-48](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L31-L48) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29)

### Data Flowsvg image

**Diagram: Bidirectional Conversion Data Flow**

The conversion process involves format-specific parsing and rendering steps. The `md2html` command uses the `markdown` library with `Pygments` for syntax highlighting, while `html2md` uses `beautifulsoup4` for HTML parsing and `markdownify` for Markdown generation.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29)

## Conversion Commandssvg image

### md2html Commandsvg image

The `md2html` command converts Markdown context files to HTML format. This conversion is useful for web-based distribution, browser viewing, or integration with HTML-based tooling.

#### Basic Usagesvg image

#### Implementation Detailssvg image

The `md2html` module is defined in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)md2html.py](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/md2html.py) and registered as a console script entry point in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py47](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L47-L47) The `main()` function handles:

1. **Argument parsing**: Input and output file paths
2. **Markdown reading**: Loads the source `.md` file
3. **HTML generation**: Converts Markdown to HTML with syntax highlighting
4. **File writing**: Saves the resulting `.html` file

The conversion leverages `contexter_utils.py` functions for consistent formatting and code block handling.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py31-47](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L31-L47) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md34](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L34-L34)

### html2md Commandsvg image

The `html2md` command converts HTML context files back to Markdown format. This conversion enables editing workflows that start with HTML-based contexts or integration with systems that produce HTML output.

#### Basic Usagesvg image

#### Implementation Detailssvg image

The `html2md` module is defined in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)html2md.py](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/html2md.py) and registered as a console script entry point in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py48](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L48-L48) The `main()` function handles:

1. **Argument parsing**: Input and output file paths
2. **HTML reading**: Loads the source `.html` file
3. **DOM parsing**: Uses BeautifulSoup to parse HTML structure
4. **Markdown generation**: Converts HTML to Markdown using markdownify
5. **File writing**: Saves the resulting `.md` file

The conversion preserves code blocks, file structure markers, and content hierarchy through intelligent parsing.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py32-48](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L32-L48) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L35-L35)

## Implementation Integrationsvg image

### Relationship to contexter\_utilssvg image

Both conversion modules utilize shared functions from `contexter_utils.py` for:

| Operation | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| File I/O | Reading and writing context files |
| Code block parsing | Identifying and extracting code sections |
| Language detection | Determining syntax highlighting requirements |
| Structure preservation | Maintaining file hierarchy markers |

This shared infrastructure ensures that conversions maintain compatibility with other Contexter commands. A file converted from Markdown to HTML and back will produce identical reconstruction results.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py24](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L24-L24)

### Dependency Chainsvg image

**Diagram: External Library Dependencies for Conversions**

The conversion system relies on four external libraries, with each direction using a distinct set:

- **Markdown → HTML**: `markdown` + `Pygments`
- **HTML → Markdown**: `beautifulsoup4` + `markdownify`

All four dependencies are specified in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29)

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29)

## Cross-Format Considerationssvg image

### Feature Paritysvg image

| Feature | Markdown | HTML | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build from directory | ✓ | ✓ | `buildcontext` vs `buildcontexthtml` |
| Reconstruction | ✓ | ✓ | `reconstructor` vs `reconstructorhtml` |
| Patch generation | ✓ | ✓ | Multiple update commands available |
| Patch application | ✓ | ✓ | `updater` vs `updaterhtml` |
| Sanitization | ✓ | ✗ | `sanitizecontext` only for Markdown |
| Smart update | ✓ | ✗ | `smartupdate` only for Markdown |

The Markdown format has more features, particularly for AI integration workflows. HTML is better suited for distribution and viewing.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

### When to Use Each Formatsvg image

**Markdown Format:**

- Development and editing workflows
- AI integration (requires `sanitizecontext`)
- Version control with smart updates
- Text editor compatibility
- Lightweight storage

**HTML Format:**

- Web-based distribution
- Browser viewing without additional tools
- Integration with HTML-based systems
- Rich visual presentation
- Archive format for documentation

**Conversion Use Cases:**

- Build in Markdown, distribute in HTML
- Receive HTML, edit in Markdown
- Maintain both formats for different audiences
- Migrate between toolchains

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

### Lossless Conversion Guaranteesvg image

Contexter's conversion system guarantees that project data is preserved across format transformations. Specifically:

1. **File paths**: Preserved exactly
2. **File contents**: Preserved byte-for-byte
3. **Directory structure**: Preserved completely
4. **Binary file handling**: Preserved identically

Only the serialization format changes. A round-trip conversion (MD → HTML → MD or HTML → MD → HTML) followed by reconstruction will produce an identical project directory.

This guarantee enables confident format switching without data loss concerns.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md3-7](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L3-L7)
